Clan Jade Falcon has employed specialist Watch units to control the civilian population of its Occupation Zone since the earliest days of the conquest, dating back to the brutal suppression known as the Culling. As the front line of Jade Falcon repression, the police show little interest in restraint or building goodwill among the occupied Lyran population. Mounted in fast wheeled vehicles and armed with a mixture of Avenger close-combat shotguns and tranquilizer guns, they swoop in to put down riots and disturbances as soon as they occur. More ominously, the police have been involved in countless nighttime arrests of Lyran nationalists over the past two decades. Inner Sphere observers have compared these operations to Capellan-style disappearances, though the Falcon police rarely make any attempt at secrecy, and the prisoners are usually publicly punished and executed.

The Ebon Keshik is a group of elite, black-clad Elementals who guard the most sacred sites on Strana Mechty. Battle armor is too bulky for these human-scale facilities, so these warriors are most commonly equipped as foot infantry in specially sculpted black body armor and armed with Clan-standard Mauser IIC assault systems. Unlikely to see combat, a warrior assigned to the Ebon Keshik has little to look forward to beyond a Trial of Position against a younger warrior and the inevitable relegation to a solahma unit. Patrolling the corridors of power on Strana Mechty is the ultimate achievement in the career of an Elemental, yet it is a tainted honor, marking the end of a warrior's useful service rather than a reward for distinguished performance.

Navies throughout history have sought dedicated marines, soldiers they can tailor to suit shipboard needs and requirements. Clan Snow Raven continues this tradition, fielding Space Marine Points drawn from warriors of all phenotypes to guard its fleet from internal threats. Unlike battle armor troops, these marines have limited mobility and are best suited to defensive operations, providing security and boarding defense on spacecraft ranging from WarShips to observation stations. Armed with Mauser IIC assault systems and fitted with marine environment suits, they can fight effectively in zero-gravity and vacuum conditions. The introduction of the Aerie power armor has raised questions about the future of unarmored marines within the Snow Raven touman, but the Aerie's prohibitive cost ensures that conventional marines will continue to fill shipboard security roles for the foreseeable future.

The Dark Caste is a mystery to nearly everybody, including the Clans themselves. Living under harsh conditions beyond the boundaries of legitimate Clan society, these outcasts limit their weaponry to whatever they can build on their own, steal, or salvage from raids. Protection for Dark Caste fighters is little better than safety equipment, with clothing, leather, and synthetic hides replacing the advanced armor kits issued to legitimate Clan warriors. Their ramshackle light vehicles are motorized transport at best. Outmatched by all but the weakest of Clan forces, Dark Caste bandits pose little direct military threat. Yet they persist, and the fear they inspire among the regimented Clans is not about what they can do on the battlefield. For warriors bound by rigid caste structures and absolute obedience, the mere existence of people who have chosen freedom over duty is deeply unsettling.

The Explorer Corps fields some of the most capable hostile environment infantry in the Inner Sphere. Formed as the armed escort component of ComStar's deep Periphery survey teams, these XCT platoons train to operate in conditions ranging from hard vacuum to crushing high-gravity atmospheres. Explorer Corps recon infantry are motorized for maximum flexibility, using tracked crawlers on high-gravity worlds and near-flying skimmers in low-gravity or dense-atmosphere environments. Armed with Mauser 960 assault systems and Hellbore assault lasers, a single platoon can provide enough firepower to discourage all but the most determined opposition. Their environment suits allow operations in toxic, irradiated, or airless conditions without degradation, making them one of the few conventional infantry formations capable of fighting on worlds where unprotected humans would die in minutes.

ComStar's battlefield data miners are a specialized signals intelligence formation deployed from mechanized hover carriers. These sensor-equipped platoons use networks of remote sensors to capture enemy transmissions and submit them for processing by Com Guard intelligence staff. While the data miners rarely crack enemy encryption in real time, their ability to measure and triangulate signal sources provides Com Guard commanders with targeting data on opposing formations. Armed with Federated-Barrett M42B assault rifles for self-defense, the platoon's primary value lies in its electronic surveillance capability rather than its direct combat power. Riding small, lightly armored hover bikes, RRF troopers combine speed with dismounted flexibility, able to cover the sprawling factory complexes that span dozens of kilometers across worlds like New Syrtis and Benet III. StarCorps Industries fields its jump assault infantry as a middle ground between fast but lightly armed rapid response forces and heavily equipped but slow static security teams. Equipped with reinforced jump packs capable of carrying a full combat load, StarCorps troopers can operate across any urban or industrial battlefield with vertical mobility that ground-bound security forces cannot match. Armed with auto-rifles and heavy grenade launchers loaded with inferno rounds, these platoons bring both conventional firepower and incendiary capability that can threaten even BattleMechs. Hachiman Taro Enterprises, the Draconis Combine electronics conglomerate founded by Chandrasekhar Kurita, fields its Extraction Force as a specialized rapid-response security unit. Each trooper is equipped with a cutting-edge one-man VTOL microcopter, granting the platoon an extraordinary degree of insertion and extraction capability. The HTE Extraction Force specializes in recovering kidnapped corporate assets and personnel from hostile situations, often completing operations before alarms are raised. Armed only with auto-rifles, the sixteen-trooper platoon carries no secondary weapons due to the bulk of their individual flight systems. This trade-off limits their sustained combat power, but the unit's value lies in speed and stealth rather than firepower. The AFFS dedicates significant resources to non-combat infantry specialties, recognizing that war produces destruction that must be managed alongside the fighting itself. The Hellfire Battalions are among the most unusual formations in any Successor State military: motorized firefighting engineers equipped to suppress battlefield blazes and protect civilian infrastructure during planetary assaults. Riding compact all-purpose vehicles, Hellfire troops are more likely to be seen carrying shovels and portable chemical sprayers than their issued Thunderstroke II gauss rifles. The guns were selected for their inability to start fires rather than for raw stopping power, a practical choice that reflects the formation's unusual dual mission of fire suppression and area security.

The AFFS Frogmen are special operations troops drawn from the blue water marine community, trained extensively in sub-surface warfare and amphibious combat. Riding electric-cell underwater sleds, these operators conduct demolitions, reconnaissance, and direct action missions in riverine and coastal environments where conventional ground forces cannot follow. Equipped with laser rifles and heavy support lasers suited for both surface and near-surface engagements, the Frogmen prove the old adage that no coastline is ever truly secure. Among the most specialized of these formations, the Cerulean Mountain Infantry trains extensively for high-altitude and rough-terrain operations. Known as the "Goat Men," these troops can establish command posts on sheer cliff faces and launch attacks from approaches that conventional forces consider impassable. Their equipment includes re-breathers that allow them to operate at altitudes where conventional aircraft and VTOLs struggle to maintain lift. The Proserpina Hussars are one of the oldest commands in the Draconis Combine, tracing their lineage to a tank regiment that fought for Shiro Kurita before the Combine existed. The brigade has maintained a close relationship with the University of Proserpina, with many officers serving as alumni and instructors at that military academy. The 201st Pesht Assault Team's Recon Battalion draws its personnel from a lesser-known graduating class at Proserpina's academy, one that has earned quiet distinction in Combine service. On first assessment the battalion's light armament of auto-pistols gives little indication of its true capability, but few enemies of the Dragon have made that mistake twice. The 201st specializes in demolition operations, fielding hover-mechanized troopers who use personal hovercraft and superior training to reach their objectives rapidly. Their combat engineering skills and demolition charges allow them to achieve results well beyond what their modest armament would suggest.

The branth is a large flying reptile native to the world of Lopez in the former Free Worlds League, described by early human explorers as a living dragon straight from Terran myth. With leathery wings, scaled hides, and sharp teeth, branths can be tamed and trained to carry one or two riders into the air, though their sheer size and strength make them dangerous even when domesticated. Their flesh and venom are poisonous to most humans, and only specially trained keepers handle them safely. The FWLM's Branth Irregulars, attached to Beta Regiment of the Fifth Legion, field platoons of seven riders armed with elephant guns. These high-powered weapons can kill any unarmored target in a single shot but are poorly suited against hardened vehicles or BattleMechs. Capable of reaching speeds near fifty-four kilometers per hour in flight, branth-mounted platoons pose little physical threat to armored targets, but the psychological effect of airborne reptilian cavalry bearing down on conventional infantry can shatter morale faster than any volley of fire.

Deployed in seven-person teams, these cybernetically enhanced commandos are drawn from military and civilian personnel across the Magistracy who have no close family or personal ties. Operating in autonomous, semipermanent cells that answer directly to the Magestrix, the Shock Troops combine fanatical loyalty with surgical lethality. Their cybernetic enhancements include Multi-Modal Cybernetic Eyes with infrared and laser targeting capabilities, full-body dermal armor plating that reduces burst-fire damage, and an Active Probe suite integrated into their optical implants. Each trooper carries four Ebony assault lasers, energy weapons built for close-quarters aggression, backed by three man-portable plasma guns that provide devastating anti-armor capability. Most troops will never encounter them on a standard battlefield, as the Shock Troops are reserved for covert operations where deniability matters as much as lethality. With the destruction of the Word of Blake's Manei Domini, the Ebon Magistrate Shock Troops may be the most dangerous commando force still operating in the Inner Sphere.

Stone's Trackers trace their origins to the 212th Nova Cat Headhunter Binary, a clandestine Clan Nova Cat unit formed during the Jihad for missions too dishonorable for conventional Clan warriors. The 212th joined Devlin Stone's coalition in 3071 and spent the remainder of the war conducting high-risk assassination, sabotage, and counterinsurgency operations against the Word of Blake. Inner Sphere personnel filled the ranks alongside the original Clanners as casualties mounted, creating a hybrid unit that embraced unconventional tactics regardless of cultural origin.

After the Jihad, the 212th was officially transferred to the Republic Armed Forces and rechristened the 212th Special Operations Battalion. The transfer stripped the unit of its BattleMech and battle armor elements over the objections of its founding commander, making the Trackers a purely infantry formation. Stone's Peace left few opportunities to maintain combat readiness, and many veteran operators retired. The Capellan Crusades provided the first real test of the rebuilt unit, and the Trackers saw heavy action during border skirmishes with the Confederation. The fighting crippled the battalion, and the 212th was officially disbanded following the Crusades. Surviving operators were reportedly distributed across RAF SpecOps Command to spread their headhunting expertise throughout the Republic's special operations community.

The horse remains the most widely used beast mount in human space, carried to hundreds of worlds during humanity's expansion across the stars. Cavalry traditions stretching back thousands of years on Terra have persisted wherever horses thrive, and many planetary militias maintain mounted infantry formations as a practical and affordable supplement to mechanized forces. Horses are fast, responsive to trained riders, and capable of operating across open terrain, grasslands, and light forest without mechanical support. On worlds where industrial infrastructure is limited or where fuel supplies are unreliable, horse-mounted infantry provide commanders with a mobile reserve that requires only fodder and water. These formations excel at reconnaissance, flanking maneuvers, and rapid pursuit, though they remain vulnerable to concentrated firepower and lack the protection of even the lightest armored vehicle.

The Odessan raxx is a massive six-legged reptile native to the Lyran world of Odessa, rivaling a Terran elephant in size. Despite their imposing bulk, raxx are remarkably docile and highly intelligent, traits that made them ideal pack animals and riding beasts. Their most extraordinary quality is endurance: a raxx can survive without food or water for up to two weeks, making them invaluable on worlds with scarce resources or harsh conditions. These qualities led to their export across countless Inner Sphere worlds, where they serve as mounts, draft animals, and military beasts of burden. Raxx-mounted infantry benefit from their animals' durability and calm temperament under fire, though the creatures become fiercely aggressive when defending their young. Military formations mounted on raxx can operate far from supply lines for extended periods, a significant advantage on the frontier worlds where they are most commonly employed.

The orca, or killer whale, represents one of the most unusual beast-mounted infantry concepts employed in the BattleTech universe. Trained orcas carry riders and equipment through aquatic environments, providing a submersible infantry platform that no conventional vehicle can easily replicate at comparable cost. Orca-mounted infantry operate in coastal waters, rivers, and open ocean, conducting amphibious raids, underwater reconnaissance, and maritime interdiction missions. The animals' intelligence and natural hunting instincts make them responsive to trained handlers, though maintaining orca-mounted formations requires access to suitable aquatic habitats and specialized veterinary support. These units are extremely rare and geographically limited to worlds with extensive water features, but where they do operate, they exploit an environment that most military planners neglect entirely.

The tabiranth, commonly shortened to "tabi," is a felinoid alien species native to the lost Free Worlds League world of Jardine. Hardy, adaptable, and possessed of an almost regal grace, the tabiranth survived its homeworld's destruction during the First Succession War because it had already been widely exported as a pet, pack animal, and riding beast. Known throughout the Inner Sphere, tabiranths are popular among nobility and animal trainers, with breeding enterprises spreading the species to dozens of worlds. Handled much like horses through reins and heel commands, tabiranths are responsive and trainable mounts that perform well across varied terrain. Military formations riding tabiranths benefit from the animals' natural agility and endurance, fielding light cavalry platoons suited to scouting and rapid maneuver on worlds where the species has established breeding populations.

The tariq (plural tariqim) is a large bipedal lizard native to the Outworlds Alliance world of Brasha. Standing just under two meters tall at the shoulder, tariqim are swift, durable, and highly intelligent. Fleshy nutrient deposits near the base of their tails sustain the animals for days in harsh conditions, while a tough, wrinkled hide and transparent inner eyelids protect against sand, grit, and desert exposure. Tariqim rival some BattleMechs and combat vehicles in overland speed, making them exceptional mounts for fast-moving infantry. The Qum'ran Guard of the Brasha Planetary Militia are the most famous tariq-mounted formation, riding their animals in service of the Outworlds Alliance. Riders form close bonds with their mounts, caring for them as family members and mourning their loss in battle. Following the Clan Invasion, Clan Snow Raven investigated the economic feasibility of broader tariq export across the Inner Sphere.
